How Do You Know the Age of Fossils and Other Old Things? | NIST
Learn how radioactive atoms can reveal an object's age, even if it's billions of years old.

ciaaw
Atomic Weight of Carbon | Commission on Isotopic Abundances ...
The radioactive ^14^C isotope has a half-life of 5730 a. It is introduced continuously to the near-surface environment of the earth by cosmic-ray reactions, from cosmic dust, and by nuclear technology. ... It should be noted that a half-life of 5568 a (the so-called "Libby half-life"), has been adopted by convention for calculations in geochronology.
